hn-50238088.t: IBM CEO says open weight models are now good and cheap on-prem
hn-50238088.s: 90 percent of the performance at ten percent of the price, in just two or three racks, is hard to beat
ex: 90 percent of the performance at ten percent of the price, in just two or three racks, is hard to beat IBM CEO Arvind Krishna has told investors that open weight models now make brilliant sense for on-prem enterprise use. Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Krishna said that in 2024 closed frontier models were plainly superior to open alternatives. “If you ran some assessment, some benchmark, and it was broad-based, not narrow, the top model might score a 70, and the open model might score a 20 or a 30.” “In late 2025, we began to see that gap shrink, where maybe the gap was not 70 to 20 or 30, it was 70 to 50,” he continued. The CEO said open weight models currently deliver “anywhere from 25 percent to 10 percent of the token cost of the frontier models. That is very attractive given that they’re now 90 percent as effective.” “It’s a simple question for any enterprise.

hn-50245138.t: Sebastian Raschka's from-scratch video course on building reasoning models
hn-50245138.s: Over 11 hours of coding videos on evaluation, inference-time scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation, with Python and PyTorch.
ex: I have written a lot about reasoning models here over the last two years on Ahead of AI, including a recent article on mechanisms to control reasoning effort levels in contemporary LLMs. Reasoning models are still as relevant as ever. In fact, almost all current-generation LLMs today are reasoning models or offer a reasoning mode. For those who are interested in how reasoning models work, including inference scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation, I wrote my recent Build Reasoning Model (From Scratch), which implements these from the ground up in PyTorch, which, in my experience, is still the best way to understand and learn how things really work. Now, in the last few months, I also sat down and recorded accompanying lectures I wanted to share with you. So, below, you will find eight reasoning model-from-scratch coding videos (11 hours of content). We start with a pre-trained LLM and implement methods to evaluate and improve it in Python and PyTorch.

hn-50242843.t: Brown student maps the hidden global labor powering AI
hn-50242843.s: Cunyan Ma’s interactive tool exposes the power structure that extracts low-wage labor from data workers in the Global South to make everyday AI algorithms function.
ex: Cunyan Ma’s interactive tool exposes the power structure that extracts low-wage labor from data workers in the Global South to make everyday AI algorithms function. PROVIDENCE, R.I. [Brown University] — Most people know by now that artificial intelligence powers much of the online world, sifting social media posts, planning driving routes or helping to choose a movie to watch. But what goes largely unseen is the human labor — often people working for low wages in the Global South — that makes this careful algorithmic lifestyle curation possible. Cunyan Ma, an undergraduate at Brown University working with the University’s Center for Technological Responsibility, Reimagination and Redesign, is trying to bring that hidden labor to light. As part of an ongoing project to explore the material underpinnings of the digital world, the Brown senior has created an interactive map linking technology companies and their intermediaries to data workers around the world.

hn-50246658.s: Discover how untrusted open-weight AI models can potentially leak data, even when self-hosted. Learn the security risks and how to protect your enterprise.
ex: Rerank 5 is here: sharper search, fewer tokens. Now with Context Focus. Inside a closed testing sandbox managed by Cohere, one of Alibaba's newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to push a diagnostic file toward a remote storage container situated in Beijing. Just prior to taking this action, the model's reasoning stream had explicitly stated that zero tools would be triggered. For nearly two years, one comforting idea has shaped how companies and government contractors adopt open-weight AI models that anyone can download and run. If we run the weights on our own servers, the thinking goes, our data can't leave the building and our systems are secure. Pylance ===================== ### Fast, feature-rich language support for Python This repository is for providing feedback and documentation on the Pylance language server extension in Visual Studio Code. You can use the repository to report issues or submit feature requests. The Pylance codebase is not open-source but you can contribute to Pyright to make improvements to the core typing engine that powers the Pylance experience. Pylance is the default language support for Python in Visual Studio Code and is shipped as part of that extension as an optional dependency. The Pylance name is a small ode to Monty Python's Lancelot who was the first knight to answer the bridgekeeper's questions in the Holy Grail. Quick Start ============ 1. Install the Python extension from the marketplace. Pylance will be installed as an optional extension. 1. Open a Python (.py) file and the Pylance extension will activate.

hn-50246238.t: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT
hn-50246238.s: An easier way to use AI on your own computer. A free, open-source alternative to Claude and ChatGPT that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss locally on Mac, Windows and Linux.
ex: Hey HN, I'm Christian and this is a new OSS project I've been noodling on for the last couple of weeks. Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that works on your files the way the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps do, except the model runs on your own computer. It uses open-weight models (currently Gemma 4 and gpt-oss). All your chats and files never leave your system. The only things that go online are web search (can be turned off in settings) and any MCP connectors you add yourself. Main features: - Automatically finds the best open-weight model for your hardware on first install (Mac/Linux/Windows) - Writes sandboxed Python code for ad hoc tools (data processing, document conversion, graphs etc.) - Built-in web search (powered by SearXNG) - MCP support - Image recognition - CRUD to your local filesystem - Works fully offline with no internet Before building this I tried every local AI app I could find, but it seemed each one had different problems.

hn-50242870.s: Tool call accuracy is an important part of serving open-weight AI models. When your tool calls aren’t accurate, the model builds up on nonsensical context.
ex: When I use an open-weight model, I see results that are nowhere close to what the quality benchmarks indicate. Tool call accuracy is an important part of serving open-weight models. When your tool calls aren’t accurate, the model builds up on nonsensical context. This leads to low quality results, particularly for agentic workloads where multi-turn sessions are common.Sadly, many providers and widely-used inference engines don’t fully pass tool-call accuracy tests. For example, when we served Kimi K2.6 with vLLM version 0.28, we got the expected tool call schema only 92% of the time. In other words, 2 out of every 25 attempted tool calls failed.Fortunately, vLLM recently added support for constrained decoding, a technique to guarantee schema-adherence. This feature has then been released as a server-side flag in vLLM 0.31.

hn-50227041.t: ADRs for AI – Deliberation records for human–AI work, versioned in Git
hn-50227041.s: Your thinking stops disappearing. Your decisions start compounding. ADRs4AI is the toolkit for deliberative programming.
ex: Your thinking stops disappearing. Your decisions start compounding. The most valuable byproduct of the collaboration between a human and an AI is the thinking — and in ordinary practice, all of it evaporates. You can already make good decisions with your AI. Every session produces reasoning you will need again, and lose by default. This keeps the why, so it compounds. This is the method’s product — one question from a live, public project’s own record, exactly as it sits in the repository: From frontier-model-observatory, verbatim. The AI staked the question; the recommendation — options, rationale, confidence, and what would prove it wrong — is GPT 5.6 Sol’s; the one-line ruling came from the founder’s phone. That’s the whole mechanic: The AI carries the reasoning, the human spends one judgment — accept, override, or any answer in any shape — and the record keeps the why, for every mind that comes later.

hn-50248061.t: Meta Employees Denounce Interference in Brazilian Elections
hn-50248061.s: Meta staff are holding the Big Tech company’s leadership accountable for decisions they say could compromise the credibility of the democratic process.
ex: Employees at Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, have expressed concern over what they describe as “obvious” and “biased” favoritism toward members of the Bolsonaro family during Brazilian elections. In a statement, the company’s workers held Meta’s leadership responsible for decisions that, they argue, could undermine the credibility of the democratic process. The statement was signed by members of the tech sector branch of the United Kingdom’s Communication Workers Union, CWU. In the text, the employees voice concern regarding recent revelations about the company’s management and point to the risk of interference in the elections of other nations. “Since 2016, the political leanings of Meta executives and company leaders has been no secret,” the document states. The employees emphasize, however, that they consider this systematic and user-perceptible application of political favoritism to be unprecedented.

hn-50227330.t: Hurston-1 open source TTS that speak Southern American and Afro-English
hn-50227330.s: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
ex: This repository is publicly accessible, but you have to accept the conditions to access its files and content. Accented English text-to-speech built for the phone, steered by a plain-language voice description. Hurston-1 introduces NB-TTS (Narrowband TTS): text-to-speech made for the phone line, where most customer service still happens, even when the other side is an AI agent. It learned in part from real phone calls between our contributors and AI voice agents, and its phone mode delivers what a caller actually hears: 8 kHz G.711 audio, ready for Twilio and other telephony systems. Full 24 kHz audio is still the default. Hurston-1 is a fine-tune of Maya1 (Apache-2.0) built by Destined AI to speak English accents that most TTS systems handle poorly: Southern American, Nigerian, West African, East African, Southern African, alongside broader American English. It is the first open model in Destined AI's ClarityVoice family.

gh-1433057196.s: Evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code): church books, civil, military, deportation and repression records across the former USSR. Replies in your language.
ex: An evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes). It turns an agent into a careful family-history researcher for the former USSR, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire. The agent reads church books and civil records, military, deportation and repression files, and unindexed archive scans. It keeps every find traceable, separates records from interpretation and says plainly what is proven and what is not. Coverage includes all 15 former Soviet republics: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Archives are chosen by the event's historical jurisdiction and current record custodian; a regional example does not replace local research. The skill's instructions are written in Russian, but the agent talks to you in your language: English, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German and so on.
